transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That grey, smelly water usually means food waste has been sitting in the bottom and starting to decompose. Let's check the most common cause first. Please take out the lower rack and twist the large filter at the bottom of the tub to remove it. Look into the sump (the hole where the filter was) with a torch—is there any food debris, grease, or glass blocking it? Also, check if you can gently turn the small impeller (fan blade) at the bottom of that hole; does it spin freely or is it stuck?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
I took the filter out and it's clean, nothing in the sump that I could see. I haven't tried turning the impeller, sorry. It's a Hotpoint HFC 3C26 W if that helps.

Since your kitchen sink was replaced last month, the most likely cause is a partial blockage at the connection point under the sink. When a new waste unit is fitted, there is usually a small plastic blanking plug inside the spigot (the hole where the dishwasher hose connects) to stop smells from the sink. If this wasn't cut out or removed, it can trap food debris that eventually washes back into the dishwasher, causing that grey smelly water. Please look under the sink at the drain hose connection and tell me if you see a plastic plug still in place. Also, run the tap and check if the sink drains quickly or slowly.

I looked under the sink. Since the new sink went in, the drain hose just lies on the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, with no high loop in it. I couldn't see a plastic plug. The sink drains a little slow, and the dirty water seems to appear after I've drained the sink.

The fact that the hose lies flat on the floor and the dirty water appears after you drain the sink suggests this is a siphoning issue. Without a 'high loop' (where the hose goes up high before dropping down), gravity pulls the dirty sink water back into your dishwasher when the sink drains. Please lift the drain hose and secure it to the underside of your worktop at its highest point, then let it drop into the waste spigot. This creates a barrier that prevents the sink water from flowing backwards. Once you've done this, run a short rinse cycle and check if the problem is resolved.
ok, I've looped the hose up high and clipped it under the worktop, then ran a short rinse. No more water in the bottom so far. Is that all I need to do?

Yes, that’s all you need to do. The lack of a high loop was allowing dirty sink water to flow back into the dishwasher when the sink drained; securing it under the worktop prevents this from happening again. Just keep an eye on your sink drainage over the next few days—if it starts draining very slowly or gurgling, that’s a sign the waste pipe itself is blocked and needs clearing before the problem returns.
